question: Which is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tirich Mir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hindu Kush, a great mountain system of Central Asia.
 
• Broadly defined, it is some 500 miles (800 km) long and as much as 150 miles (240 km) wide.
 
• The Hindu Kush Himalayan region spans Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.
 
• It traverses about 5 million square kilometres and hosts a large and culturally diverse population.
 
• It is considered the Third Pole (after the North and South Poles) and has significant implications for climate.
 
• It contains vast cryospheric(cold) zones and is also the world’s largest store of snow and ice outside the polar region.
 
• SIGNIFICANCE__-
 __
 
• The significance of the Hindu Kush mountain ranges has been recorded since the time of Darius I of Persia.
 
• Alexander the Great entered the Indian subcontinent through the Hindu Kush as his army moved past the Afghan Valleys in the spring of 329 BCE. 
 
• He moved towards the Indus valley river region in the Indian subcontinent in 327 BCE, his armies building several towns in this region over the intervening two years.
 
• The subcontinent and valleys of the Hindu Kush remained unconquered by the Islamic armies until the 9th century, even though they had conquered the southern regions of the Indus River valley such as Sind. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda Devi:** It is the second-highest mountain peak in India, located in the Garhwal Himalayas. It is known for its challenging terrain and stunning beauty.
 
• **Udren Zom:** This mountain peak is situated in Sikkim, India. It is a popular trekking destination offering breathtaking views of the Himalayan ranges.
 
• **Karakoram:** This mountain range extends across parts of Pakistan, India, China, and Afghanistan. It is home to several of the world's highest peaks, including K2.
